page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured under KVM virtualization, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is fixed at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). The processor integrates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, along with support for vector instruction extensions including AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI.

Hardware provisioning on the ecs.c5.xlarge does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators. Persistent data storage relies on attached network volumes. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the lower performance brackets relative to modern cloud infrastructure. In stress-ng testing, it achieves 1103.19 in single-core and 2934.5 in multi-core metrics, both falling into the lower quartile. Geekbench scores show 987.0 for single-core and 2173.0 for multi-core performance. Memory throughput is similarly constrained, measuring 20.58 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB read operations and a PassMark memory score of 1246.19. From a resource-efficiency perspective, the instance trades peak computational throughput and memory bandwidth for dedicated x86 core allocations in modest workloads.

The ecs.c5.xlarge instance is technically aligned with low-intensity, non-bursting compute tasks. Primary workload fits include entry-level web serving, staging servers, basic microservice hosting, small-scale Redis caching, and modest batch execution pipelines that do not demand extensive memory capacity or high-speed local disk operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory on a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz with a 35 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512 instruction sets. The instance includes no local storage and no GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage and providing a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing yields modest results, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2173.0 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 2934.5. Qualitatively, it offers steady dedicated CPU resource allocation without the overhead of oversized memory pools. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, small background workers, and entry-level computational tasks.
